A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BAD-PODS and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of two-group SIR and moving-source localization, including information-gain and design-quality results over 50 seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds ecological growth experiments, oracle comparisons, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The EIG and gradient estimators, stochastic-gradient design optimization, and nested particle-filter updates remain unchanged. The detailed Algorithm 1 is retained in the appendix. The oracle is an added comparator, not a replacement for BAD-PODS.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix G add ecological growth with harvesting. Unlike the retained SIR and moving-source tasks, this scenario makes designs affect both transition dynamics and observations, materially broadening the capabilities actually evaluated.

E2.justification: v1 compares BAD-PODS with random and static designs. v2 adds an adaptive grid-search oracle to both original experiments and the new ecological experiment, providing a substantive reference for the quality of gradient-based design optimization.

E3.justification: Added oracle evaluations use 500 candidate designs for SIR and ecology and a 25-by-25 grid for moving-source localization. The ecological experiment introduces T=20, M=N=200, and K=200 settings. Stated settings for the original experiments remain unchanged; newly documented tuning searches do not establish changed protocols there.

E4.justification: v2 adds a runtime and memory comparison for SIR at T=150 and an ecological design-distribution analysis in Figure 7. Existing allocation and pointing-error diagnostics also gain oracle comparisons. These are targeted additions to computational and behavioral analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 seeds, bootstrap 95% BCa confidence intervals, and boxplots showing medians and interquartiles. Expanding the BCa abbreviation and changing numerical intervals do not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds oracle and ecological results, and Section 5.1 adds computational-cost measurements. Original SIR scores remain unchanged, but moving-source BAD-PODS results are revised: at T=50, TEIG changes from 1.740 [1.551, 2.096] to 1.733 [1.658, 1.840] under unchanged stated settings. For ecology at T=20, v2 reports 2.545 for BAD-PODS, 2.621 for the oracle, and 2.344 for random design.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds mathematical definitions of harvesting dynamics and saturated observations. The original EIG derivations, five assumptions, and consistency proof are retained. Newly added Equation (4) also introduces a localized inconsistency: its likelihood integral uses a filtering distribution conditioned on y1:t rather than the predictive distribution before observing y_t.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claimed gap to the joint challenge of partial observability and fully online inference. The introduction adds an explicit constant-memory-in-horizon claim and emphasizes long-horizon feasibility. The central estimator, inference, and consistency contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 explains pointing-error outliers through low signal-to-noise and weak identifiability. It also interprets ecological gains plateauing, small advantages over static design at short horizons, and intermediate harvesting effort through signal strength, population depletion, and observation saturation.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F newly document hyperparameter-search ranges, selection criteria, and Adam momentum settings. Oracle grids, ecological implementation settings, and runtime and memory consumption are also supplied. This substantially expands reproducibility information, although Appendix G omits the numerical catchability coefficient q. The code link and hardware description are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Koch (2016) for sensor tracking and Zhou et al. (2009) for ecological modeling. It removes Allen (2008), Arino and van den Driessche (2003), Chatzilena et al. (2019), and Sheng and Hu (2005). The main related-work discussion and positioning against existing BED approaches remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, motivation, NPF explanation, and experimental descriptions within the existing section structure. It adopts 'sequential BED' terminology, corrects the erroneous SIR expansion, consolidates model details in appendices, and adds an impact statement. Most method and proof prose is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes from two side-by-side model blocks to three stacked blocks with an oracle column. Figures 1, 2, 4, and 5 gain oracle displays, and Figures 6–7 are new. The document template, typography, headers, and appendix layout change throughout; the abbreviated main-text algorithm disappears while the detailed algorithm remains.

improvement.justification: The ecological experiment tests previously untested design-dependent dynamics, while oracle comparisons and resource measurements strengthen validation of the existing method. Expanded tuning information improves reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the new likelihood-conditioning error, incomplete ecological settings and unresolved equation references, and Section 5.2's claim of highest TEIG despite higher oracle scores in Table 1.
